research_basis: Baymard 2026 mobile ecommerce benchmark: 75% of benchmarked sites rated mediocre; mobile requires careful overview and simple interaction.
Baymard product-list research: product lists materially affect product-finding success; horizontal areas should not hijack vertical scrolling.
2022 scarcity meta-analysis: scarcity effects vary by scarcity type and context; scarcity should be aligned to the actual product and purchase stage.
2026 Journal of Retailing: artificial supply scarcity can reduce perceived sincerity when quantities are unexpectedly low; genuine availability and guarantees mitigate the problem.
2025 Psychology & Marketing: scarcity can increase urgency but social and temporal cues can also drive alternative shopping; product-based fixed scarcity is safer for a unique digital asset.
guardrails: Never claim a remaining count that is not derived from durable placement capacity.
Never use an invented countdown timer.
Never imply traffic, impressions, rankings or sales are guaranteed.
Payment remains separate from human publication approval.
